codes.title: Pneumonia, organism unspecified
codes.rationale: The clinical findings of fever, productive cough with thick green sputum, coarse crackles, and bronchial breathing at the right base support a provisional diagnosis of pneumonia. GDL-016 (effective 2026-01) requires radiographic or ultrasound confirmation for a definitive assignment, but GDL-017 (effective 2023-07) allows clinical findings to support a provisional assignment where imaging is unavailable. The later guideline (GDL-016) is preferred due to its more recent effective date, but the provisional status is retained due to the absence of imaging.

evidence.quote: 4 days of fever and cough, now bringing up thick green sputum, sharp right-sided pain on deep breath. Temp 38.6, RR 24... Coarse crackles at the right base with bronchial breathing there.
Effective with this revision, a definitive pneumonia assignment rests on radiographic or point-of-care ultrasound confirmation of consolidation recorded in the encounter.
Fever, productive cough and focal crackles with dullness to percussion over the affected zone are sufficient to assign community-acquired pneumonia in the primary care setting.

confidence_rationale: The clinical findings strongly suggest pneumonia, but the absence of imaging (required by GDL-016) precludes a definitive assignment. The provisional status reflects the need for confirmation via imaging to rule out other conditions (e.g., lung abscess or pleural effusion).
would_raise_confidence: Radiographic or ultrasound confirmation of consolidation at the right base.
would_lower_confidence: Development of symptoms or signs inconsistent with pneumonia (e.g., sudden onset pleuritic pain with absent breath sounds suggesting pneumothorax).

data_quality_flags: Conflict between GDL-016 (2026-01) and GDL-017 (2023-07) regarding imaging requirements for pneumonia. GDL-016 is preferred due to its later effective date, but GDL-017 supports clinical diagnosis in the absence of imaging. The provisional status resolves this conflict.

codes.title: Gout
codes.rationale: The presentation of sudden severe pain, swelling, and erythema of the first metatarsophalangeal joint, with systemic features (fever, shivering), is classic for gout (GDL-013). However, the absence of synovial fluid microscopy (due to no service on site) and serum urate testing precludes definitive confirmation. The provisional assignment is supported by the typical clinical picture in a patient with diabetes, a risk factor for gout.

evidence.quote: Woke two days ago with severe pain and swelling at the base of the right big toe. Joint now red, shiny and so tender he cannot bear the weight of the bedsheet on it. Temp 38.3 today and reports feeling shivery overnight.

Sudden severe pain, swelling and erythema of the first metatarsophalangeal joint waking the patient from sleep, with exquisite tenderness to light touch, is the classic gout presentation... Where fever accompanies an acutely swollen joint, synovial fluid microscopy and culture establish the diagnosis, and the aspiration result is the basis for the assigned entry.
